### MechWarrior / BattleTech (`mechwarrior`)

Written before any mechwarrior unit is coded, from the BattleTechWiki's unit role pages (Scout, Sniper, Striker and Juggernaut, and the Unit Roles category), its Master Unit List, BattleMech and InfoBoxBattleMech pages and a sample of 'Mech pages, the MechWarrior Online Wiki's 'Mech pages, and the official MechWarrior Online and MechWarrior 5: Clans sites. Checked again in the R4 prep on 11 November 2026: the same wiki pages (the Unit Roles category through the wiki's API; the Centurion, Timber Wolf, Atlas and Jenner pages; the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Centurion and Centurion CN9-A pages), both MUL sites, mwomercs.com (home, Game menu, store, patch notes and one news post) and mw5clans.com (home, news index and three posts).

- **Designation: the unit role.** The rulebooks the role pages cite (the Introductory Rulebook of Classic BattleTech, the two Alpha Strike books and Campaign Operations) define a set of battlefield roles, and the Master Unit List (MUL), Catalyst Game Labs' official unit database, gives units their role (the role pages link MUL searches by role). Read the role of the MUL entry for the model researched as its designation for roles step 1, and cite the MUL as kind official.
- **Which roles name ours.** The Unit Roles category lists fourteen: Ambusher, Attack Fighter, Brawler, Dogfighter, Fast Dogfighter, Fire Support, Interceptor, Juggernaut, Missile Boat, Scout, Skirmisher, Sniper, Striker and Transport. Scout is our scout label, Sniper is an alias of marksman, and Transport is our transport label. Fire Support means firepower, so it names no role, and the other ten are none of our labels or aliases. Marksman still has its coding rule: a Sniper whose long-range guns are not in our sniper family fails it, and step 1 goes on. The category still holds the same fourteen on 11 November 2026 (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Category:Unit_Roles; role pages such as https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Scout_(unit_role) and https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Sniper_(unit_role)).
- **Where to read it.** The BattleTechWiki's Master Unit List page (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Master_Unit_List) says MUL 2.0 replaced the old site on 31 August 2026. The masterunitlist.info unit links on the wiki's pages now fail (the Centurion's answered HTTP 404 on 11 November 2026), and the new site (https://masterunitlist.battletech.com/) refused this session's requests; one polite request from the page reader on 11 November 2026 was refused again (HTTP 403). The BattleTechWiki's 'Mech pages do not give the role: InfoBoxBattleMech has no role field (its seldom-used Use field is the wiki's words, and the template's usage notes no longer list it), and the role pages describe each role without listing units (their MUL search links still point at the old site). A text search of the wiki found no 'Mech page that names its MUL role, and no other official page on the web that prints a unit's role was found. When no coder can read the MUL, step 1 finds no official line: go on to step 2.
- **So no official role text can be read for this game today.** Every mechwarrior unit starts at roles step 2 (not a fighter), then step 3 (reach: siege only for a lobbed main weapon that reaches long or further, such as artillery; marksman only for our sniper family), then step 4 (see Strong-against below), then step 5. Leave the MUL out of sources and say in an uncertain entry at roles/primary that it could not be read.
- **Technical Readouts.** A readout's own text on a design (its Capabilities section and the rest) is official, but the BattleTechWiki does not copy it: its Description and Weapons and Equipment sections retell it in the wiki's words, with page references, so they are not official text. The infobox's weight class (Ultralight, Light, Medium, Heavy, Assault, Superheavy) is filled in from the mass; it is the armour map's key, not a role. MechWarrior 5: Clans has a readout of its own, sold with the game's Deluxe (Digital Extras) edition and not on the web; its patch notes of 6 February 2026 say the readout pages for the Wolves of Tukayyid 'Mechs are still to come.
- **The piloted games.** No official 'Mech role or description line was found for MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5: Clans. Neither official site (mwomercs.com, mw5clans.com) has 'Mech pages, the game-manual link of the MechWarrior Online site leads back to its overview page, and the 'Mech descriptions on the MechWarrior Online Wiki are its own words. Checked on 11 November 2026: MechWarrior Online's Game menu offers only Overview (at /game/user-guide, the same text as /game), Patch Notes and Download; its store lists packs through a script, so the page reader sees none of them; and a news post that announces a 'Mech pack (Perseus Booster Pack, 19 October 2026) is official text but uses sales words and names no role. mw5clans.com has news, DLC, resources and media pages only. MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries has an in-game 'Mech database with descriptions (its Ashes & Ascension patch notes of 6 October 2026 mention it), but Mercenaries is not a counted title, so that text never counts. Their patch notes are official text: mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes and the Steam news feed for app 342200, and the release notes in the news on mw5clans.com. The newest are https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes/3116 (20 October 2026) and, for Clans, https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update (6 February 2026); every later post on the mw5clans.com feed is about MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries. A role word in patch notes names a role only by the roles word list's own rules: the February 2026 notes call the Arrow IV a support weapon, and support meaning firepower names none.
- **Strong-against and weak-against:** none of these sources has such lines. Roles step 4 therefore rests on the game data or on a main weapon that can hit nothing else, and no page read gives a weapon extra damage against a kind of target. The bracket tags in the BattleTechWiki's weapon Type field (anti-infantry on the Machine Gun, Flamer and Plasma rifle) and the wiki's prose calling those weapons deadly to infantry are the wiki's words: they count only for the roles.secondary label clause (see Words in brackets, under MechWarrior damage), never for step 4. A target list that is short only because MechWarrior Online has almost nothing but 'Mechs to shoot at does not count as hitting nothing else (roles.secondary).
- **Sides.** A design is one entry whichever side fields it, so the rule that official text must hold for every side's version only matters for an archetype recorded once for several designs.

### MechWarrior / BattleTech (`mechwarrior`)

Written in the research run's batch preparation, before any mechwarrior unit is coded, from the BattleTechWiki's BattleMech, Physical Attacks, Jump Jet, Heat Sink, OmniMech, Mechanized Battle Armor, List of Design Quirks and MechWarrior 5: Clans pages, and the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Beginners Guide: Interface/Basics, Heat Sinks, Heat Scaling, Critical Hit, Armor, Module and Quirks pages. The MechWarrior Online Wiki pages are old (last edited between 2012 and 2021), so check MechWarrior Online facts against its patch notes. The counted titles are the tabletop designs, MechWarrior Online and MechWarrior 5: Clans (see Series games). Checked again in the R4 prep on 11 November 2026 against those pages, the BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans/BattleMechs and Sensors pages, the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Beginners Guide: Goal of the Game page, MechWarrior Online's overview page (https://mwomercs.com/game) and patch notes of 20 October 2026 (https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes/3116), and two official MechWarrior 5: Clans posts: the Elementals preview of 8 April 2025 (https://mw5clans.com/news/2025/04/144-elementals) and the newest Clans patch notes, of 6 February 2026 (https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update).

- **Basic controls** (throttle, turning the legs, torso twist and centring the torso, full stop, powering down and up, targeting an enemy to see its weapons and damage and to lock guided missiles, weapon groups, chain fire and alpha strike, zoom, night and heat vision): every 'Mech. No pattern. Torso twist is how a biped 'Mech aims, not an ability; quads cannot twist without a design quirk. The mount proposal follows the aim-models tie-break, which counts a torso that twists only partway as limited arc.
- **Orders to teammates** (no pattern): MechWarrior 5: Clans gives the player a Command Wheel and a Battle Grid to direct the rest of the star, and in MechWarrior Online one player per team can place battle-plan markers. These are basic orders: leave them off.
- **Heat** (resource heat; no pattern): every 'Mech gains heat from firing, moving and jumping, and sheds it through heat sinks; past its limit it shuts down. In MechWarrior Online the pilot can override the shutdown for a few seconds, at the risk of internal damage and an ammunition explosion; MechWarrior 5: Clans has an override too (its patch notes of 6 February 2026 mention the voice line that announces it). Code heat as the resource on every 'Mech; shutdown and override belong to it and are not abilities. MechWarrior Online's heat scaling ("ghost heat") adds extra heat when too many of certain weapons fire at once: mention it in the summary of a weapon it affects (the patch of 20 October 2026 still tunes it, raising the LRMs' penalty). Equipment that dumps heat on a key (a coolant pod and the like) belongs to the design that carries it.
- **Ammunition** (resource limited-ammo, where that field's rule fits): ballistic and missile weapons feed from ammunition carried in the 'Mech. The only refill during a fight in the pages I read is MechWarrior 5: Clans' ammo caches, tagged in scan mode. MechWarrior Online's Event Queue sometimes runs an Unlimited Ammo modifier (its overview page): a game-mode rule, left off.
- **Locations and critical hits** (armour model zonal): every 'Mech's armour and structure are split by location (head, torso sections with front and rear armour, arms, legs). Once a location's armour is gone, hits can wreck the weapons and equipment inside it, ammunition included, before the location itself is destroyed. Code zonal on every 'Mech; it is built into the armour, and the model's examples name this game. Code directional as well: every torso section has front and rear armour, and standard designs put less on the rear. Leave it off only when a source shows the rear as thick as the front. Ammunition-protection equipment (CASE) belongs to the design: mention it in armour.notes. The front and rear split is on the MechWarrior Online Wiki's Armor page (each torso location divides its armour between the two). No page read gives a design's armour by location (the BattleTechWiki's infobox names only the kind of armour), so when no cited page shows the rear values, say so in armour.notes.
- **Physical attacks** (tabletop; no pattern): as its build allows, a 'Mech can punch with its arms, push, kick, charge, or swing something it has picked up, and one with jump jets can make a death-from-above attack. These come with being a 'Mech: leave them off weapons and abilities. A melee weapon the design carries (a hatchet and the like) is a weapon of our melee family. No page read shows 'Mech melee in MechWarrior Online (its wiki's FAQ, written before launch, says none was planned) or in MechWarrior 5: Clans; the melee variants on some BattleTechWiki pages (the Centurion's CN9-P with a mace) come from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries, which is not counted.
- **Jump jets** (mobility trait leap; pattern leap): not game-wide. Only designs that mount them can jump; record them on those units. Jumping heats the 'Mech and makes it harder to hit, but spoils its own aim (Jump Jet page). Since Wolves of Tukayyid, MechWarrior 5: Clans' jets also push the 'Mech the way the pilot steers (BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans page): say so in the leap ability's summary. Clan BattleMechs in MechWarrior 5: Clans can fit or drop jets in the MechLab, a loadout choice: record jets only when the stock model mounts them.
- **Speed and electronic equipment**: not game-wide. MASC, triple-strength myomer and superchargers, and electronics such as ECM, active probes, TAG and Narc, belong to the designs that carry them; record them on those units (patterns.md gives MASC as an overclock-self example, and an always-on ECM is the jammer trait). The standard sensors and the electronic-warfare features every 'Mech has, which make it harder to lock onto (the BattleMech page), give no sensor trait. Neither does the basic sensor data every combat unit's targeting and tracking system can share with friendly units (BattleTechWiki's Sensors page). Clan BattleMechs in MechWarrior 5: Clans can add or drop MASC in the MechLab: code the stock model.
- **Variants, OmniMech configurations and refits** (no pattern): a design's variants, an OmniMech's pod configurations and MechLab refits are chosen before a battle, never during one, so they are not abilities or modes. Code the model researched; other configurations follow the armament rules for loadout picks, or go in notes. (Refitting one OmniMech location takes about half an hour, by the OmniMech page; MechWarrior 5: Clans' Clan BattleMechs also swap engines of the same type between missions.)
- **Design quirks** (no pattern): the tabletop's optional quirks and MechWarrior Online's per-variant quirks mostly change numbers: put those in notes. Record a quirk as a passive only when it adds a mechanic. A quirk that changes rolls or numbers, for the 'Mech or for units near it (Command 'Mech, Distracting), is a number change: notes only. The Rumble Seat quirk (a second seat for a passenger) was dropped from the BattleMech Manual: it gives no passenger seat.
- **Progression** (no pattern): MechWarrior Online's skill tree and MechWarrior 5: Clans' 'Mech XP upgrades and pilot skills improve a 'Mech outside the fight. Bands use the stock 'Mech; notes can name them.
- **Consumables and call-in strikes** (side-wide powers): in MechWarrior Online the player fits consumables (artillery and air strikes, Cool Shot coolant and others) into a 'Mech's consumable slots. They are the player's kit, not the design's: leave them off. Since Wolves of Tukayyid, MechWarrior 5: Clans lets the player call artillery strikes onto a point picked on the Battle Grid (BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans page; patch notes of 6 February 2026): a side-wide power, left off too.
- **Elemental Point** (MechWarrior 5: Clans, Ghost Bear: Flash Storm DLC; side-wide support, no pattern on any 'Mech): in that DLC's missions a Point of Elementals fights beside the player's Star. It attacks nearby enemies by itself, can be sent at a chosen target, finishes off an enemy 'Mech whose head armour is gone, and comes back after a short wait when wiped out; enemy Points jump onto a 'Mech and cling to it, doing some damage (Elementals preview). It belongs to no 'Mech design: leave it off every 'Mech. If an Elemental is coded as a unit, record its latching on and its finishing blow on that unit.
- **Scan mode** (MechWarrior 5: Clans; no pattern): every pilot can switch to a mode, with weapons unable to fire, for hacking turret controls, disarming mines, opening locks and tagging salvage and ammo caches. Leave it off.
- **Repair and salvage** (no pattern): technicians repair 'Mechs between missions in MechWarrior 5: Clans, and the pages describe no repair during a fight. Leave it off.
- **Riding battle armour** (tabletop; carry-passengers would be the pattern): most OmniMechs have handholds that let friendly battle armour ride them into battle (six suits at most, twice that on superheavy 'Mechs), and other 'Mechs can carry riders only when the riders have magnetic clamps. The riders hang on outside rather than sit in seats, so give the 'Mech no passenger seats and leave the riding off it; say in crew.notes that an OmniMech can carry riders. If battle armour is coded, record riding on it as its own (see Other uncertainties). Riders add a little protection to the OmniMech that carries them (OmniMech page), and clamps slow a standard 'Mech that carries riders (Mechanized Battle Armor page): crew.notes can say both. MechWarrior 5: Clans' Elementals do not ride friendly 'Mechs in the pages read.
- **Capturing bases** (a game-mode rule, no pattern): the capture points of MechWarrior Online's Assault and Conquest modes. Other game-mode rules stay off as well: MechWarrior Online's Event Queue modifiers (Unlimited Ammo, Extra Armor) and Faction Play's four 'Mechs per match, and MechWarrior 5: Clans' Arena and Horde modes (Trials of War).

notes.other_notes:
- **Sites to cite for this game, one page each, plant test of 11 November 2026** (run in this prep; every planted passage was flagged):
  - www.sarna.net (BattleTechWiki; read through https://www.sarna.net/wiki/api.php): https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Centurion_(BattleMech), 5 of 5 (browser view).
  - mwo.fandom.com (MechWarrior Online Wiki; read through https://mwo.fandom.com/api.php): https://mwo.fandom.com/wiki/Centurion_CN9-A, 5 of 5 (the browser got HTTP 403, so the wiki's rendered page from its API stood in).
  - mwomercs.com (official MechWarrior Online site, for patch notes): https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes/3116, 5 of 5 (browser).
  - mw5clans.com (official MechWarrior 5: Clans site, for patch notes and DLC pages; new in this prep): https://mw5clans.com/news/2026/02/180-mw5-clans-patch-notes-and-update, 5 of 5 (browser).
  - Not needed and not tested: Steam news (MechWarrior Online Legends is app 342200, MechWarrior 5: Clans app 2000890; only single posts can be read). Not citable: masterunitlist.battletech.com, which refuses requests (HTTP 403).
- **Versions.** MechWarrior Online is patched every month (list at https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes, each patch at /game/patch-notes/<number>, newest 3116 of 20 October 2026): take the newest patch at coding time and name it in sources[].version. Quirks change almost every month (that patch changed several), so never take a quirk from the MechWarrior Online Wiki; quirks are numbers for notes anyway. MechWarrior 5: Clans' newest patch notes are those of 6 February 2026; its DLCs are Trials of War (November 2024), Ghost Bear: Flash Storm (May 2025) and Wolves of Tukayyid (December 2025).
- **The mw5clans.com news feed also carries MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries** (Chaos Reign in May 2026 and Ashes & Ascension in October 2026 are Mercenaries DLCs). Check that a post is about Clans before citing it.
- **MechWarrior 5: Clans lets the player pilot only Clan 'Mechs** (OmniMechs, and from Ghost Bear: Flash Storm some Clan BattleMechs). Inner Sphere 'Mechs appear only as enemies, with models taken from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries (BattleTechWiki's MechWarrior 5: Clans/BattleMechs, Non-playable table). That table names models and nothing of how they play, so MechWarrior Online decides how an Inner Sphere design plays. Its OmniMechs keep their tabletop armour values (MechWarrior Online lets players trade pod space for armour), raised only by upgrades or modular armour pods. The BattleTechWiki tags its MechWarrior 5: Clans pages as apocryphal (outside the setting's canon); that does not stop them being sources for how the game plays.
- **Speeds.** The infobox's speed field is the top running speed without speed equipment, cut to whole km/h on the pages read (Centurion 64, Timber Wolf 86, Atlas 54, Jenner 118); the registry's 64.8 is the Centurion's prose figure, and the cut never moves a band. MASC, triple-strength myomer and supercharger speeds have fields of their own: they go in the ability or in notes, never in speed_raw. The step-1 Speed bullet's 118.8 km/h for the Jenner is worked out from its movement; its page prints 118 (over 118 in the prose), fast either way.
- **Weapon pages.** Of the weapons read, only the Autocannon/10's infobox shows an Extreme Range field (16-20): compare long ranges. A blank Minimum Range field does not mean none: the LRM 10's is blank, while the Long-Range Missile page speaks of the minimum range of Inner Sphere LRMs. Titles to ask the API for: Particle Projector Cannon, Gauss rifle, Arrow IV Artillery, Long Tom Artillery Piece, Anti-missile system, Plasma rifle, Target Acquisition Gear, Narc Missile Beacon, Machine Gun, and one page per launcher size (LRM 10, SRM 6); the family pages Long-Range Missile and Short-Range Missile have no infobox and so no Type field.
- **Apocryphal Variants.** 'Mech pages list video-game variants in an Apocryphal Variants block after the canon ones (the Centurion's CN9-P from MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries, its CN9-ON from MechWarrior Online Legends). Code the canon model researched; a Mercenaries variant never fills a field, and a MechWarrior Online Legends variant goes in notes at most.
- **Roles, in practice.** With no readable MUL role, step 1 never decides. The armour map makes every listed 'Mech medium or heavier, and raider needs light or no armour (roles.primary step 5 and roles.secondary step 4), so no 'Mech becomes a raider that way. Scout needs an information part with an in-game basis, and sight bands here are medium proposals, so it comes only from such a part, as TAG or a Narc beacon coded with the mark trait, or an active probe that finds hidden units (detector). Expect most armed 'Mechs to end as assault at step 5, fast light 'Mechs included. That follows from the rules as written; whether fast light 'Mechs should read as raiders or scouts is a question for Mustafa at the rule-fix round.

So the Centurion itself, and every 4/6 'Mech with a cut infobox, would code slow, while 4/6 'Mechs whose page keeps 64.8 code medium. The rounding claim is right only as arithmetic: no page states it, but 5 walking MP gives 81 there and 86.4 on the tabletop.
verdicts.evidence: data/vocab/speed-bands.json: slow is 0.7 up to but not including 1; medium is 1 to 1.5. The infobox speed field keeps the decimal on some pages (Goliath 64.8, Raven 97.2) and cuts it on others (Centurion 64, Jenner 118). MechWarrior Online and MechWarrior 5: Clans do not round the running speed up (Timber Wolf: 86.4 on the tabletop, 81 in MechWarrior 5: Clans); use the tabletop figure.

Fire Support is a fighter role (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Fire_Support) and Transport is for airborne or aerospace craft such as DropShips and airships (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Transport); Attack Fighter, Dogfighter, Fast Dogfighter and Interceptor belong to the same group. So a 'Mech's MUL role could name ours only as Scout or Sniper, and Transport never applies to a 'Mech.

The notes miss https://www.sarna.net/wiki/BattleMech_Combat_Categories, which is in the BattleMech Roles category. It lists example 'Mechs per role: Atlas, Hunchback and Cyclops as juggernauts; Jenner and Commando as strikers; Catapult and others as missile boats; Spider and others as scouts; Panther, Awesome and others as snipers. It is an edited copy of pages 51 to 54 of the CBT Introductory Rulebook, which the page itself calls out of date. It is not a designation, not the MUL and not a faithful copy, so it must never give a step-1 line. The notes should say so, because a coder will find it beside the role pages.

MechWarrior Online has official per-'Mech pages that the notes say do not exist: https://mwomercs.com/packages/<name> (e.g. /packages/perseus, linked from the Perseus post) and https://mwomercs.com/legends/<name> (e.g. /legends/Onyx). They give tonnage, engine, max rating, top speed, armour total, heat sinks, jump jets, ECM and MASC capability, and weapons and hardpoints by location. They have no role line, but they are official sources for MechWarrior Online play facts, such as the hardpoint type that decides damage step 4. The Onyx page also shows a 50-ton Centurion with a 200 engine moving at 64.8 kph: a current, official speed check that the 2014 wiki page cannot give. The Machine Gun's infobox gives 2 plus 2D6 against infantry, and the Flamer's gives 2 plus 4D6 (the burst-fire table on page 217 of Total Warfare): https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Machine_Gun and https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Flamer, Damage field. candidates.name: Raven (RVN-3L)
candidates.teaches: Electronic warfare as a whole job. This 35-ton light carries a Guardian ECM suite, a Beagle active probe, TAG and a Narc launcher beside light guns (Sarna infobox and Weapons and Equipment). The ECM hides teammates near it and spoils enemy locks inside its 180 m bubble, the Narc sticks a homing pod on a target so friendly missiles track it even out of sight, TAG paints a target for quicker locks, and, in MWO, the probe cancels one enemy ECM nearby. It is the partner of every missile boat and, through its bubble, their hard counter. The old MWO wiki adds a counter loop: a probe, a TAG beam from outside the bubble, wrecking the torso that holds the suite, and (to check in patch notes) a PPC hit. Coding caution: the game-wide note makes an always-on ECM the jammer sensor trait (MWO's key only flips it to a counter mode that cancels enemy ECM), and the Granularity rule gives TAG and Narc, as weapons, the weapon trait mark; the two patterns below apply where the coder records them as abilities.
candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: playable in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists an MWO hero version, the Huginn). Not in MechWarrior 5: Clans, whose 'Mechs are all Clan designs. Any tabletop force can field it.
candidates.repeats: No unit in data/units links jam-sensors or mark-target yet; the registry notes already name MWO's Guardian ECM as the jam-sensors example. Stealth armour appears only on the RVN-4L variant (notes).
candidates.shooter_note: A fragile, quick spotter who wins fights without topping the damage chart: hold the bubble over the team's push, tag the enemy's big guns for the missile players, and run when anything catches it alone.

candidates.name: Firestarter (FS9-H)
candidates.teaches: A weapon that attacks the enemy's heat instead of its armour. Four flamers (one of them aimed backwards from the centre torso), two medium lasers, two machine guns and six jump jets on a 35-ton light (Sarna infobox and Weapons and Equipment). The Flamer page types the weapon as heat-inducing and anti-infantry: it does little harm to 'Mechs and vehicles but raises their heat, kills infantry, and sets trees alight; the Firestarter's Description has crews burning woods to break up an enemy, shield a withdrawal or stop a chase. It turns the game-wide heat gauge into something an enemy can fill for you, so the target must hold fire or risk a shutdown.

new_mechanics.summary: Pour heat, or another self-limiting gauge, into an enemy so it must stop firing, slow down or shut down, instead of taking health off it; it could fold into disable-machine as a heat variant.

candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists MWO hero versions such as the Ember) and in MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries; not in MechWarrior 5: Clans. Any tabletop force; Sarna says every Great House used it.
candidates.repeats: Fire left on the ground is the flamethrower family's zone trait, which many C&C units already carry; the heat attack is the new part. The old MWO wiki caps flamer heat at 90% of the target's limit, so a forced shutdown is a tabletop effect unless current MWO patch notes say otherwise.
candidates.shooter_note: A close-range harasser that cooks heavier 'Mechs into silence and torches infantry; it must jump in, burn and get out, because it loses any straight trade.

candidates.name: Piranha
candidates.teaches: The iconic counter to infantry and battle armour. Clan Diamond Shark built this 20-ton sprinter (151 km/h) around twelve machine guns; its only other guns are two ER medium lasers plus one ER small laser (Sarna infobox and Description). The MWO wiki adds that its machine guns do little damage but are strong at wrecking components once armour is gone. Its Weapons and Equipment section says the gun array wipes out unarmoured troops in seconds and that a Star of them, hunting as a pack, tears through a 'Mech's rear armour almost at once. It gives the generator a cheap counter-pick to the Elemental and a reason to guard your back.
candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists MWO-made variants and a sale page); not on MechWarrior 5: Clans' list of playable 'Mechs. Any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: Machine-gun anti-infantry units are common in data/units; the twist is the pack that hunts rear armour and battle armour. The Nova is also called a battle armour killer on Sarna, so the lead may keep only one of the two for that job.
candidates.shooter_note: A buzzing flanker that circles behind slow 'Mechs and shreds infantry, and folds against armour from the front.

candidates.name: Hatchetman (HCT-3F)
candidates.teaches: A carried melee weapon and a head that flies away. A 45-ton medium with an autocannon/10, two medium lasers, four jump jets and the first 'Mech-sized hatchet (Sarna infobox and Description), meant for city ambushes that cut enemies apart at point-blank range. The hatchet is a weapon of our blades family with melee delivery, apart from the game-wide punches and kicks; Sarna's Hatchet page says it outhits a punch and adds no heat. No production 'Mech before it had a full-head ejection system: rockets blast the whole head clear as an escape pod, and its computer usually steers the short flight toward friendly forces (Weapons and Equipment; Full-Head Ejection System page). That is a memorable death rule for a shooter: pilot-eject, with the pod flying to safety.
candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists the MWO hero Tinman) and in MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries; not in MechWarrior 5: Clans. Any tabletop force; first built in the Lyran Commonwealth to a design from a Federated Suns mercenary team.
candidates.repeats: The urban ambush overlaps the UrbanMech (left out). The game-wide note says pilots come back in the next drop, so the head pod is a twist for notes or for on_death pilot-eject. The late HCT-5DT variant adds triple-strength myomer, which doubles physical attack damage once the 'Mech runs hot (notes only).
candidates.shooter_note: Jump onto a rooftop, drop behind a heavier 'Mech and chop; when it falls, the player rides the head pod back toward friends.

candidates.name: Phoenix Hawk LAM (PHX-HK2)
candidates.teaches: Three forms instead of two. A Land-Air 'Mech switches between a 'Mech, an aerospace fighter with modest fuel, and a hybrid AirMech mode that moves like a wing-in-ground-effect craft (Land-Air BattleMech page, Combat abilities). The twist is that hits to its limb actuators, hips or gyro can jam the conversion and lock it in its current form, so its versatility is also its weak spot (Construction). The Phoenix Hawk LAM is a 50-ton Star League design, thinly armoured, whose guns are one large laser, two medium lasers, two machine guns; it was the largest LAM able to use AirMech mode (its own page).
candidates.skirmish: Tabletop only (era rules in Interstellar Operations); Sarna names no MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5 version.
candidates.repeats: transform is in data/units (Mecha Tengu, Olga Morozova, William Mason); this adds a third, in-between form and a conversion that damage can jam.
candidates.shooter_note: A raider that flies in fast, drops to AirMech to skim and shoot at ground level, and lands to fight as a 'Mech; take a hit to the legs and you are stuck in whatever form you had.

candidates.name: Nova (Black Hawk) Prime
candidates.teaches: Firepower capped by its own heat. A 50-ton Clan OmniMech with five jump jets and twelve ER medium lasers whose Prime makes nearly double the heat its sinks can shed (Sarna Weapons and Equipment), so the full volley is a bet against a shutdown. It shows the generator a unit whose limit is the resource rather than cooldowns, and MechWarrior Online's heat scaling adds extra heat when too many of one weapon fire together (MWO wiki, Heat Scaling).
candidates.skirmish: Playable in MechWarrior 5: Clans (campaign with four-player co-op, plus the free Trials of War arena mode with PvP) and in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists an MWO hero). Any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: Heat is game-wide and coded on every 'Mech, so this is a strengths-and-weaknesses lesson more than a pattern; drop it if the Firestarter and the Coolant Truck already carry enough heat play.
candidates.shooter_note: A jump-in brawler with one enormous volley: fire everything and you may freeze in the open, so the player paces shots and picks the moment.

candidates.name: Catapult (CPLT-C1)
candidates.teaches: Missile fire support as a team job. A 65-ton second-line 'Mech with two LRM-15 racks, four medium lasers for anything inside the racks' minimum range, and four jump jets (Sarna infobox and Weapons and Equipment). It supports friends from beyond 600 m, has only eight reloads per rack and so leans on supply, and lacks arms and anti-infantry guns. MWO's LRMs lock on, can fire indirectly on targets teammates share, and have a 180 m minimum range (MWO wiki: LRM 15, and the ECM page on shared targeting). With the Raven it forms BattleTech's spotter-and-shooter pair, and an ECM bubble is its counter.
candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: in MechWarrior Online (Sarna lists MWO hero and legendary versions) and in MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries; not in MechWarrior 5: Clans. Any tabletop force; the Capellans hold most of them.
candidates.repeats: Siege units exist (Iron Harvest Nakovalnya and others); the twist is lock-on missiles that need a teammate's eyes (the spotter hook) and lose to ECM.
candidates.shooter_note: Sits behind the brawl raining missiles on whatever teammates light up; a light 'Mech that slips inside its minimum range is its nightmare.

candidates.name: Barghest (BGS-1T)
candidates.teaches: The four-legged body plan as BattleTech plays it. Sarna's BattleMech page (Chassis Types, Quadrupedal) says quads gain stability and can sidestep (lateral shift), and the game-wide note says their torso cannot twist without a quirk, so this walker strafes and aims by facing instead of turning its guns. Its LB 20-X autocannon fires either a solid round or a cluster round that works like a giant shotgun shell, and if that one gun jams or runs dry only two ER large lasers remain (Barghest page, Weapons and Equipment). Katherine Steiner-Davion ordered it as a frightening four-legger in the Atlas tradition.
candidates.skirmish: Tabletop only; Sarna's page names no MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5 version.
candidates.repeats: legs-multi is already on Iron Harvest walkers and the RA3 Sickle, and switch-weapon-mode on the Hammer Tank and Terror Drone (the patterns notes fold ammo types into it). Its new part, the fixed torso with a sidestep, is a word-list gap (a mobility trait), not a pattern.
candidates.shooter_note: A crab-walking gun line: strafe sideways with the guns fixed forward and swap between solid and cluster rounds by range.

candidates.name: Timber Wolf (Mad Cat) Prime
candidates.teaches: The iconic Clan OmniMech and the cleanest case of a unit sold as configurations. A 75-ton frame with 27.5 tons of pod space that the Prime fills with two LRM-20s, two ER large and two ER medium lasers, a medium pulse laser and two machine guns (Sarna Weapons and Equipment); other configurations swap the pods before battle. The generator should treat these as loadout picks, not abilities (game-wide rule), and the unit sets the Clan medium-to-long-range baseline.
candidates.skirmish: Playable in MechWarrior 5: Clans and in MechWarrior Online; any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: Teaches little the other candidates do not (its LRMs repeat the Catapult); kept as the iconic Clan heavy and the loadout-pick example, and the first to trim if the lead wants mechanics only.
candidates.shooter_note: The all-rounder heavy a new player buys: pick a pod set before the match and fight at mid to long range.

candidates.name: Atlas (AS7-D)
candidates.teaches: The juggernaut with a guard on its back. The 100-ton AS7-D is slow and carries an autocannon/20 for brawling, an LRM-20 that can fire directly or indirectly, an SRM-6 and four medium lasers, two of which point to the rear to punish flankers (Sarna infobox and Weapons and Equipment). Every part of it, down to the skull-like head, was shaped to scare the enemy. For a shooter it teaches rear-arc guns as the answer to circle-strafing, and a slow boss unit. Faction: a Star League design built to Kerensky's brief and used by every Great House; Clan warriors refitted captured ones as the Atlas C, so shared is the alternative.
candidates.skirmish: Multiplayer: in MechWarrior Online (Sarna names MWO versions) and in MechWarrior 5: Mercenaries; not on MechWarrior 5: Clans' playable list. Any tabletop force.
candidates.repeats: Super-heavy bosses exist (RA1 Mammoth Tank, Generals Overlord); the rear-facing guns and the fear design are the twist. The command variant (AS7-D-DC) trades the rear lasers for a command console (a number change). The Dire Wolf repeats the juggernaut for the Clans.
candidates.shooter_note: The team's walking fortress: slow, the most armour, a gun for every range, and rear lasers that make flanking it costly.

candidates.name: Executioner (Gladiator) Prime
candidates.teaches: Speed bursts that can cripple you, on an assault frame. MASC lifts this 95-ton OmniMech from 64.8 to 86.4 km/h in short bursts, and four fixed jump jets let it leap (Sarna Executioner page). Sarna's MASC page says heavy use can damage the leg actuators, and the MWO wiki says overuse locks them, first slowing the 'Mech and then possibly stopping it. A Gauss rifle and two ER large lasers fight at range; the old MWO wiki adds that the Gauss rifle itself explodes when destroyed. It is a heavy that keeps up with 'Mechs far lighter than itself.
candidates.skirmish: Playable in MechWarrior 5: Clans (Sarna's bibliography and its Trials of War hero) and in MechWarrior Online (Sarna cites the MWO sale page for its Clan Heroes II pack). Any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: overclock-self is in data/units (Kirov, Voltaic Tank) and the patterns notes already name MWO's MASC as its example; the twist is that the price lands on its own legs (zonal self-harm) and that an assault does it. The Fire Moth (MASC on the fastest light) was left out as a repeat.
candidates.shooter_note: An assault that sprints and jumps to choose its range; overuse the sprint and its legs give out at the worst moment.

candidates.name: Dire Wolf (Daishi) Prime
candidates.teaches: The Ultra autocannon gamble. The 100-ton Prime pairs four ER large lasers, four medium pulse lasers and an LRM-10 with two Ultra AC/5s, and its pilot must ration fire to stay cool (Sarna Weapons and Equipment). Sarna's Ultra Autocannon page says the gun fires at twice the normal rate, burning ammunition and heat faster and shaking the 'Mech at full rate; the old MWO wiki gives each double shot a chance to jam the gun for a few seconds. A fire-rate gamble the generator does not have yet, on the heaviest Clan OmniMech.

new_mechanics.summary: Fire a weapon at double rate on demand, accepting a chance that it jams and falls silent for a few seconds; it may belong in the weapon-trait list rather than the patterns.

candidates.skirmish: Playable in MechWarrior 5: Clans and in MechWarrior Online; any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: It repeats the Atlas as a juggernaut; only the Ultra autocannon gamble is its own, so the lead may keep one of the two.
candidates.shooter_note: A slow gun platform whose damage spikes when the player gambles on double fire, then goes quiet while a gun is jammed.

candidates.name: Elemental
candidates.teaches: Power-armoured infantry that hunts 'Mechs. Each suit jumps 90 m, fires a missile pack it can drop once empty, and has a battle claw that rips armour off a 'Mech or grips an OmniMech's handholds (Sarna Elemental page, Weapons and Equipment; Battle Claw page). In MechWarrior 5: Clans an enemy Point leaps onto the player's 'Mech and latches on to damage it, while a friendly Point can finish off any 'Mech whose head armour is gone and comes back a while after being wiped out (Sarna's MechWarrior 5: Clans page; the official Flash Storm news post). On their own side, suits ride OmniMechs into battle on handholds that open to a friendly IFF signal, six suits to a 'Mech (Mechanized Battle Armor page).

new_mechanics.summary: Cling to the outside of a friendly vehicle or walker to ride it into battle, exposed rather than seated, then jump off to fight; the carrier gives no seats and may slow down.

candidates.skirmish: Not a piloted unit in MechWarrior Online or either MechWarrior 5; MechWarrior 5: Clans' Ghost Bear Flash Storm DLC adds Points as AI companions and as enemies. Any tabletop Clan force.
candidates.repeats: infest-vehicle repeats the RA3 Terror Drone, a drone; this is a squad of soldiers that also rides friends and finishes a weakened 'Mech. Its counters are the Piranha's machine guns and the leg-mounted anti-personnel pods on 'Mechs. Sarna has no page under the obvious titles (Swarm Attack, Leg Attack) for the tabletop rules on those attacks.
candidates.shooter_note: A squad player who leaps onto an enemy 'Mech's back and pries it open, or hitches a ride on a teammate's OmniMech to the front.

candidates.name: 135-K "Lifesaver" Coolant Truck
candidates.teaches: Support that works on the heat gauge. Built for the Draconis Combine, this 30-ton wheeled truck connects hoses to overheated 'Mechs (one for a light or medium, two for a heavy or assault) and flushes their heat out with liquid nitrogen; its two turret flamers can be switched to spray nitrogen and cool a 'Mech very fast (Sarna Description and Weapons and Equipment). A hooked 'Mech is exposed, but battlefield custom has enemies leave it alone while it holds fire. With the Firestarter it makes heat a resource both sides can push.

new_mechanics.summary: Hook up to or spray a teammate to drain its heat, or another overload gauge, quickly so it can fire again sooner, while the cooled unit stands exposed; it could fold into resupply-allies as a variant.

candidates.skirmish: Tabletop only (Technical Readout: 3025 and 3039); no MechWarrior Online or MechWarrior 5 version, and Sarna describes the cooling in design text only, with no game rule.
candidates.repeats: Support vehicles exist in data/units (healers, resupply); cooling an ally's heat is new. The J-27 Ordnance Transport (ammunition resupply) was the alternative and is left out.
candidates.shooter_note: A pit-stop medic for 'Mechs: drive up behind the line, hose down an overheating teammate so it can fire again, and switch the nozzles to flame infantry that rush you.

candidates.coverage_note: Fourteen candidates: twelve 'Mechs spread three per weight class (light Raven, Firestarter, Piranha; medium Hatchetman, Phoenix Hawk LAM, Nova; heavy Catapult, Barghest, Timber Wolf; assault Atlas, Executioner, Dire Wolf), one battle armour (Elemental) and one combat vehicle (135-K Coolant Truck). Factions: Inner Sphere 8 (liao Raven and Catapult, steiner Hatchetman and Barghest, kurita Coolant Truck, plain inner-sphere Firestarter, Phoenix Hawk LAM and Atlas) and Clan 6; no davion or marik design. Classes: walker, infantry and vehicle, with flight only through the LAM's fighter form. Roles: scout, siege, support, anti-infantry, anti-armour, area-denial, raider and assault. Price tiers have no source (has_costs false); weight class stands in (light low to assault very high). Mechanics: electronic warfare and spotting (Raven) with the missile boat it serves (Catapult); heat from three sides (inflicted by the Firestarter, suffered by the Nova, removed by the Coolant Truck); a carried melee weapon and a flying head pod (Hatchetman); a three-form transform that damage can jam (LAM); a fixed-torso quad with a slug-or-cluster autocannon (Barghest); MASC whose cost lands on the legs (Executioner); the Ultra autocannon jam gamble (Dire Wolf); rear-facing guns and fear by design (Atlas); battle armour that latches on, finishes a stripped 'Mech and rides friendly OmniMechs (Elemental) with its counter (Piranha); Omni pods as loadout picks (Timber Wolf). New ids proposed: overheat-target, vent-ally-heat, ride-on-ally, double-tap-jam. Left out on purpose: UrbanMech (urban ambusher, repeats the Hatchetman), Highlander (Gauss and jump jets on an assault, repeats the Executioner; its burial is a game-wide physical attack), Hatamoto-Chi and C3 (only on variants, and Sarna says MWO lacks C3), Kodiak (juggernaut repeat), Fire Moth (MASC repeat), Goliath (second quad), Hunchback (its lesson is zonal damage, game-wide), stealth armour and triple-strength myomer (variants only: Raven RVN-4L, Raven RVN-3X, Hatchetman HCT-5DT), J-27 Ordnance Transport (a second support truck), VTOLs, hovercraft such as the Savannah Master and aerospace fighters (no mechanic beyond class and speed that data/units lacks; strafing passes repeat the RA1 Yak and the Aurora), QuadVees, tripods and superheavies (late eras, rarely seen), IndustrialMechs and naval units. Sites to cite, one page each for the copy-check: www.sarna.net (https://www.sarna.net/wiki/Raven; plant test passed on 11 November), mwo.fandom.com (https://mwo.fandom.com/wiki/Electronic_Countermeasure_(ECM); passed on 11 November), mw5clans.com (https://mw5clans.com/news/2025/04/144-elementals; new to the batch, needs the plant test; the page reader reads it as plain text), and mwomercs.com (https://mwomercs.com/game/patch-notes; 4 of 5 on 11 November, the miss a cookie notice), needed because the MWO wiki pages are old (ECM modes, flamer heat cap, Ultra autocannon jam, Gauss rifle).
